title: David vs. Goliath: Maryville Esports Takes on Korea’s Greatest Team Ever Assembled
summary: David vs. Goliath: Maryville Esports Takes on Korea’s Greatest Team Ever Assembled  Maryville University
content:
Threeindividualswill step onto one of the biggest stages in the history of competitive gaming. On Saturday, September 19, JunHao“AoJune“Chen, Jeremiah “ScaryJerry“Leathe, and Ryan “Zyko” Jung will wear the red, white, and blue in an internationalLeague of Legends(LoL)showdown against South Korea’s national teaminafriendly.

This isn’t just any roster; it’s a Maryville reunion on the international stage:

2,500 fans packed into the stunning Busan Cinema Center, the electric atmosphere of a Korean esports crowd, and a broadcast beamed exclusively on Disney+ across North America, Europe, and Southeast Asia. The match will be hosted by the Korea e-Sports Association (KeSPA), which invited the United States as one of just two international opponents alongside Vietnam to sharpen its squad for the Asian Games. KeSPA is rolling out the red carpet, covering housing, meals, ground transportation, and practice facilities for the entire delegation.

This tier-two, semi-pro roster was assembled by Nick “Inero” Smith, head coach of the USA Esports LoL program and a veteran of the North American professional scene. He’ll be joined on the bench by Aiden “Niles” Tidwell, Maryville’s head LoL coach, traveling with the delegation to assist the coaching staff. Dan Clerke, national team manager for USA Esports, andMaryville University’s director of esports,is coordinating the entire operation. While North America’s top league sits in the middle of its playoffs and couldn’t release its players, the door swung open and Maryville’s finest walked through.

“Being a part of this means the world to me,” said Aiden Tidwell. “I love my country, so having the chance torepresentthem is something I will always cherish. Also, playing against some of the greatest players of all time makes this a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity —we’llmake the most of this trip.”

title: Strong, South Korea! Bouncing Back From Game 1 Loss to Secure 3-1 Victory Against Vietnam
summary: Strong, South Korea! Bouncing Back From Game 1 Loss to Secure 3-1 Victory Against Vietnam  Inven Global
content:
On the 20th, Day 2 of the 'LoL National Team Evaluation Match' between South Korea and Vietnam took place at the Busan Cinema Center. After a shaky start with a Game 1 loss, South Korea claimed three consecutive games to complete a 'loss-win-win-win' series victory. In particular, they demonstrated immense resilience in Game 3 by pulling off a massive comeback from a heavily disadvantaged position.

South Korea suffered a shock loss in Game 1. Taking the lead through precise macro play, South Korea seemed to control the momentum after securing the Baron. However, after 'Zeus' Choi Woo-je's Gragas was caught out, they repeatedly forced teamfights at a disadvantage, leading to crushing defeats. As a result, the Cloud Soul went to Vietnam, allowing them to complete the turnaround.

In Game 2, South Korea successfully struck back. South Korea and Vietnam engaged in a fierce contest, exchanging blow for blow. Unlike the previous game, South Korea steadily stacked dragon buffs to pressure Vietnam. This translated into teamfight victories at the third and fourth dragons, and after scoring a clean Ace in the final top-lane fight, South Korea secured the win in Game 2.

Game 3 saw a dramatic comeback from South Korea. Starting with a solo kill, 'Zeus' on Camille stacked up multiple kills in consecutive top-lane skirmishes to become massively accelerated. However, Vietnam continued to score plays on the opposite side of the map, and ahead of the third dragon, they successfully claimed Camille's shutdown. Following this, South Korea accumulated losses against Vietnam's aggressive macro. A decisive stealth Baron attempt also ended in an Ace for Vietnam.

However, around the 32-minute mark, a miraculous teamfight unfolded. As the main force absorbed a turn of Vietnam's offensive, Camille engaged to take down 'Dire's Ahri, while 'Keria' Ryu Min-seok's Poppy knocked away 'Eddie's Ezreal, creating a critical gap in Vietnam's damage output. Sweeping up four kills, South Korea followed up a Baron steal by 'Canyon's Nocturne by taking the Elder Dragon as well, advancing with the Elder buff to destroy Vietnam's Nexus.

In Game 4, 'Hizto's Trundle actively ganked lanes to snowball the early game. However, with appropriate responses from 'Zeus's Gnar and 'Faker's Anivia, South Korea steadily accumulated kill points of their own. Although the kill score remained tied, all other metrics favored South Korea. Monopolizing dragons and towers alike, they widened the lead to over 4,000 gold.
